title: What rule does this number machine follow?
description: A machine takes two inputs and gives one result. A rule is tried on every pair, then written in words and as an expression in the letter-numbers a and b.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rule is trusted only after it matches every pair, and then it is written for the letter-numbers a and b. Watch for students who say the machine only adds the inputs.

source: A machine gives: inputs 5 and 2 give 5; 8 and 1 give 7; 9 an
video_script.why: A learner sees that a rule is trusted only when it matches every pair, and is then written for a and b.
video_script.substitution: the book's machine with four pairs of inputs and results, and the letter-numbers a and b
video_script.anchor: the number machine of the book, tried on four pairs of inputs
video_script.wrong_answer: the machine adds the two inputs
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the machine adds the two inputs. Adding gives seven for five and two, but the machine gave five, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The expression is eigh plus b minus two.
maths_rules: rule: add the two inputs and take away 2
in words, 2 is subtracted from the sum of the two numbers
inputs a and b: a + b - 2
Keeko test: only adding gives 5 + 2 = 7, but the machine gave 5
video_script.design: The machine stays on the board; one rule is tried on each pair in turn, said in words, and then written with letter-numbers.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number machine with two inputs and one result; pairs 5, 2 to 5; 8, 1 to 7; 9, 11 to 18; 10, 10 to 18

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the machine is drawn
marks.pairs: the four pairs of inputs and results appear beside the machine
marks.ask: a question mark appears on the machine

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is the next puzzle in your book, where the machine takes two inputs and gives one result.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Five and two give five, and eight and one give seven. Nine and eleven give eighteen, and ten and ten give eighteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What rule does the machine follow?

beats.on_screen: the machine and the four pairs stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one rule for every pair; first input a, second input b; trust a rule only when it matches every pair

marks.rule: one rule is shown acting on every pair
marks.names: the first input is labelled a and the second input is labelled b

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The machine follows one rule for every pair of inputs.
<bookmark mark='names'/>We call the first input eigh, and the second input b.
<bookmark mark='trust'/>We trust a rule only when it matches every pair.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four pairs of inputs with their results.

beats.on_screen: To find: the rule, and the expression for the inputs a and b

marks.find: the words rule and expression are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the rule, and write the expression for the inputs eigh and b.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: try the rule add the two inputs, then take away 2

marks.try: the rule add the inputs, take away 2 is written beside the machine

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step one, try a rule: add the two inputs, and then take away two.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, test the first pair, where five plus two minus two is five, which matches.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Test the second pair, where eight plus one minus two is seven, which matches.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the third pair has nine plus eleven minus two as eighteen, which matches.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The last pair has ten plus ten minus two as eighteen, so the rule fits all four pairs.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: two is taken away from the sum of the two numbers; for the inputs a and b the machine adds them and takes away 2

marks.words: the rule is written in words
marks.letters: the first input becomes a, the second input becomes b, and the rule is written with them

narration: <bookmark mark='words'/>Step four, say the rule in words: two is taken away from the sum of the two numbers.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>For the inputs eigh and b, the machine adds them, and takes away two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The expression is eigh plus b minus two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the machine
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the machine only adds, struck out; 5 + 2 = 7, but the machine gave 5

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the rule only add
marks.gap: 7 and the machine's 5 appear side by side and do not match

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the machine adds the two inputs. That sounds right, as the results grow when the inputs grow.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try the first pair with adding alone, where five plus two is seven.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>But the machine gave five for that pair, not seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The machine also takes away two, so adding alone is not the full rule.
